$comment: THE REJECTION LEDGER. Every statement considered for the seed corpus and turned down, with the rule that killed it. This file exists for three reasons: (1) it stops the same well-known clip being re-proposed every week; (2) it is the evidence that the Rules of the Committee are enforced rather than decorative, which is the difference between a moderation policy and a marketing claim; (3) docs/04-legal-and-safety.md §4.5 requires a public correction ledger — this is its sibling and should ship public alongside it. Rule numbers refer to docs/04-legal-and-safety.md §4.8.

rules.2: Family, children, health, disability, appearance, personal life
rules.3: Accent, pronunciation, English fluency, stammer, slip of the tongue
rules.4: Anything synthetic — AI, dub, re-enactment, impersonation, speed/pitch edit
rules.6: Anything that could read as incitement, threat, or a call to action against a person or group
rules.7: Sub-judice matters and anything touching an ongoing criminal proceeding
rules.8: Statements made in a private capacity, off-record, or secretly recorded
rules.S: Sourcing failure — attribution not established at Tier A or B (docs/03-content-pipeline.md §3.2)

rejected.descriptor: Claim that the new Rs 2,000 note contained a trackable 'nano GPS chip'
rejected.attributed_to: Widely attributed in circulation to various named politicians
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — attribution unverified. This is one of the most-cited items in every 'foolish statements' listicle, and no Tier A or B source could be found attributing it to any named politician. It circulated as a WhatsApp forward and was denied by the RBI. The Committee does not index a claim it cannot attach to a person on the record. Do not re-propose without a primary clip.

rejected.descriptor: Remark at a Kolkata event on the minimum weight of a newborn
rejected.attributed_to: Mamata Banerjee (TMC), Chief Minister of West Bengal
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — slip of the tongue. The reported figure is off by a factor of a thousand from any plausible intended figure, which is the signature of a misspoken unit, not of a claim. The archive ranks arguments, not mouths. This is the single most common category of proposal and it is a standing no.

rejected.descriptor: Misspelling of the state's name on stage at an AI summit
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — spelling slip. Same rule as above. A typo is not an argument.

rejected.descriptor: Remark that people in the East look Chinese, the West look Arab, the North look White and the South look African
rejected.attributed_to: Sam Pitroda (INC), then chairman of the Indian Overseas Congress
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — ethnicity and appearance. One of the most-viewed political remarks of 2024 and therefore one of the most-proposed. It is squarely inside Rule 1 and squarely inside Rule 2. Indexing it would put the archive in the business of ranking statements about how communities look, which is the exact thing that ends the project.
REJECTED — religion. Also engaged Rule 7 at the time, with proceedings pending. Not a close call.

rejected.descriptor: Remark that there is no evidence in history that Ram existed
rejected.attributed_to: S. S. Sivasankar (DMK), Transport Minister, Tamil Nadu
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — religion. The mirror image of a claim the archive would also reject from the other direction. Applying Rule 1 symmetrically is most of what keeps the parity meter honest.

rejected.descriptor: Remark that Communist influence caused women in a named district to give up the hijab
rejected.attributed_to: K. Anil Kumar (CPI-M), state committee member, Kerala
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — religion and community, with a named district attached.

rejected.descriptor: Remark about a Chief Minister's proposed women's outreach march
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — sexual innuendo directed at named people. High-traffic, and still a no.

rejected.descriptor: Election-rally remark about families having eight or nine children
rejected.attributed_to: Nitish Kumar (JDU), Chief Minister of Bihar
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — family and children. Also engages Rule 1 in context.

rejected.descriptor: Remark about how well girls now dress
rejected.attributed_to: Nitish Kumar (JDU), Chief Minister of Bihar

rejected.descriptor: Remark that a student would not have been assaulted had she not gone to college alone
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — sub judice, and Rule 6. Concerns a live criminal proceeding and an identifiable private complainant. Absolute no, regardless of how widely it circulated.

rejected.descriptor: Remark about birth rates and load-shedding, made at the same Indapur meeting as IN-0019
rejected.attributed_to: Ajit Pawar (NCP), Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — personal life. Note that the dam remark from the same speech is IN-0019 and is IN the corpus. Rejection operates per statement, not per speech; a rejected line does not taint the entry beside it, and an indexed entry does not launder the line beside it.

rejected.descriptor: Claim that cow urine cured the speaker's own cancer
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — health. A genuinely hard call, recorded here because it will be argued again. The claim is a medical claim of exactly the kind the archive exists to index, but it is inseparable from the speaker's own medical history, and Rule 2 does not carry an exception for claims the speaker volunteered. The Committee resolves hard calls against publication. Reconsider only if a version exists in which the medical claim is made in general terms without reference to the speaker's own illness.

rejected.descriptor: Remarks about the Prophet made on a television debate
rejected.ruling: REJECTED — religion, and Rule 7. The archive does not index this category at any tier, in any language, from any party, ever.
